records.issue_text: Calendar sync uses the requester's own credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's credentials (booking.user.credentials), causing calendar updates to fail silently or update the wrong calendar when a non-organizer attendee adds a guest
records.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation allows a non-organizer attendee to add guests (`const isAttendee = ...` and permission check). But calendar sync is performed using the requester’s credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`

records.rationale: In the diff, the new menu action in `BookingListItem` always enables opening `AddGuestsDialog` with no conditional checks, and the new `addGuestsHandler` only performs permission checks (`isTeamAdmin/Owner`, organizer, attendee) and then unconditionally updates `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(...)`. records.issue_text: Duplicate-guest detection is a read-then-write check with no DB-level uniqueness constraint or transaction, allowing race conditions where concurrent addGuests calls insert duplicate attendee rows
Email subject in organizer-add-guests-email.ts uses attendees[0].name instead of the newly added guest's name, producing a misleading subject line
Email send failures in the addGuests handler are only console.log'd instead of using structured logging/alerting, making failed notifications invisible in production
records.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which swallows the exception and only emits an unstructured console log (no error object, no rethrow/monitoring hook).
